overview: This Senate resolution designates May 2025 as 'National Wildfire Preparedness Month.' It notes that wildfires have grown larger and more severe, that fire seasons now last much longer in many places, and that most wildland fires are caused by people. It encourages federal, state, local, and tribal governments, along with community groups, to raise awareness and prepare for wildfires. It also supports educational efforts on prevention steps such as fire-resistant building materials, clearing flammable brush, early warning systems, protecting health from smoke, and safe evacuation of people and their animals. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on June 16, 2025.
for: Supporters say raising awareness of simple steps like hardening homes and planning evacuations can help communities reduce wildfire losses.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and that it was agreed to after the month it designates had already ended.
